content.comment_body: My [product_name] is connected to an MQTT broker and sends data correctly. However, I want to stop it from sending the $logotime message every 10 seconds since this uses unnecessary resources. Is this possible? Thanks.
No, you can't access the time and date on your [product_name]. Only remote devices, such as another [product_name], a different controller, or an HMI can access these details.

To clarify, I’m not trying to access time and date, but I want to prevent the [product_name] from sending this information automatically every 10 seconds once MQTT is active. So far, I haven’t found any setting to change this.
You should consider starting a support request.

Hello, One possible improvement is to check the MQTT data table where you configure how often data is transferred. Adjusting those settings might change how frequently $logotime is sent by the [product_name]. Hope this helps.

Hello all, I'm working with a [company_name] [product_name] and facing the same issue of automatic time and date messages being sent every 10 seconds via MQTT. I know there’s no direct way to access time and date, but I just want to stop this auto-send behavior. I haven’t found any setting to control or disable it. Has anyone solved this or found a workaround? Suggestions are welcome! Thanks in advance.
Submit a support request for further assistance.
Hi. Hope you’re well. Did you find a solution to this issue? I also want to stop that payload every 10 seconds.

I understand you are using [product_name] version [version_no] for MQTT communication. Another option is to use Node-Red and a Raspberry Pi to filter the data before it reaches MQTT. If the [product_name] can’t stop this directly, an external solution may be needed.

Has anyone been able to solve this? I don’t get why $logotime isn’t shown in the cloud data tab, or why there’s no way to configure triggers for MQTT publishing/subscribing. The hello/ping timing doesn’t appear in MQTT setup, and this isn’t the standard for MQTT clients.
This forum can't provide an answer for this. You'll need to contact [company_name] directly by submitting a support request.

I'm facing the same challenge. Even with cloud data set to 'On Change,' information is sent every 10 seconds, and the timestamp is incorrect—always 10 hours ahead of local time—even though the correct time zone is set in [product_name]. I expected data only when bits change, but I need to add extra filtering and correction at the receiving end. If anyone knows a solution, please share!

Has anyone found a solution or more information about this? I have the same issue. Setting the cloud data transfer period to 5 minutes leads to 29 empty JSON packets (just timestamp) sent every 10 seconds, plus one actual data packet. The empty packets are frustrating.

I asked support about this a while ago. The answer was that sending timestamp messages every 10 seconds is a standard feature of [product_name] and cannot be changed. It’s documented in the manual: '[product_name] publishes time data every 10 seconds.'

analysis.insight_summary: Users report that their [product_name] devices send recurring internal time messages ($logotime) via MQTT every 10 seconds. This behavior is non-configurable in current firmware and consumes resources unnecessarily. Users are frustrated because this message flow cannot be controlled or disabled from standard configuration menus, which they consider inconvenient for their applications.
analysis.user_expectations: Users expect to have the ability to configure or disable the periodic $logotime transmission over MQTT, aiming for greater control and efficiency in device communication.
